universalAgentRuntime.role: C04 service placement and UAR public run/A2A surfaces

librefang.role: C04 BossFang base and current UAR provider/A2A/task surfaces

rules: Full-run delegation is distinct from native BossFang execution and UAR model-provider access.
UAR exclusively owns the delegated token, model and tool loop.
BossFang owns the parent workflow, delegation control and correlation receipt without replaying delegated tools.
Every delegated trace identifies universal-agent-runtime as executor.
The qualified admission tuple is reserved before execution begins.
The same key and digest return the same native receipt without another run.
The same qualified key with a different digest is refused with admission_digest_conflict.
A lost response becomes admission-unresolved and is reconciled without replay.
Identity and placement derive from the authenticated C04 service binding, never payload claims.
BossFang retains a durable correlation receipt and projects UAR state without becoming a second executor or task authority.
Lookup and control require authenticated owner, selected UAR instance and target binding in addition to native identity.
UAR approval identities and tool-admission evidence remain authoritative.
Unknown effects remain effect-unconfirmed and are never automatically replayed.
Steering continues the same governed active task and never creates an implicit replacement run.
Detach changes observation and does not request cancellation.
Cancellation requested, acknowledged and terminal states remain distinct.
Cleanup and effect uncertainty remain explicit until proven settled.
Every receipt advertises retention mode and expiry.
Unsupported recovery is explicit and never represented as success, ordinary not-found or automatic replay.

process-ephemeral.scope: one UAR process lifetime and its advertised in-process retention window
supports: qualified idempotent admission while the process remains alive
native task observation and control while retained

unsupportedSemantics.required: refuse admission with a stable reason
unsupportedSemantics.optional: return explicitly unsupported in the receipt and never label enabled or enforced

wire.encoding: snake_case JSON on the UAR wire; camelCase on BossFang's public API

authentication.workspaceHeaderRequired: all admission, reconciliation, task, stream and control routes; capability descriptor is workspace-independent
authentication.identitySource: verified token principal and source-instance claims

admissionRequest.targetSelectorRule: deployment_binding_id selects the admitted C04 binding
admissionRequest.digestRule: UAR computes sha256 over canonical JSON containing the run body and normalized x-uar-workspace-id
admissionRequest.credentialRule: opaque references and existing run-API host input shapes only; resolved secrets are forbidden

wire.reconciliation: capture runtime_epoch before admission, then GET by admission_id with the same authenticated owner and required workspace header; an epoch change maps to recovery-unsupported and performs no replay
eventRules: cursor is monotonic within one task
cursor gaps and expiry return typed postures

acceptanceScenarios.expected: UAR alone owns the delegated loop and each admitted effect occurs once
same key and digest recover the original task/run with no duplicate execution
changed digest under the same qualified key is refused with admission_digest_conflict and without another run
observation disconnect does not cancel; reconnect resumes from the advertised cursor
cancellation reaches the exact UAR run and acknowledgement remains distinct from terminal settlement
one UAR approval identity is decided once and the same native task continues
both products expose effect-unconfirmed and perform no automatic replay
wrong owner, workspace, target or instance cannot observe or control the task
C04 identity, profile, capabilities, endpoint roles and opaque credential references are admitted before execution
explicit recovery-unsupported with no success claim or resubmission
explicit expired posture preserves qualified correlation identity
native BossFang and model-provider execution retain their existing executor ownership

dependencies.c02: protected-effect admission and uncertain external outcomes
dependencies.c03: lossless definitions and enforced runtime semantics
dependencies.c04: service identity, placement, endpoint roles and credential references
